# Plan for 3.3 and 3.4

> **Status (2026-11-04):** 3.3.0 is done: negation in grounding (#168), the comparison and the LlamaIndex.TS guide (#170), AI SDK grounding middleware (#171), test-runner matchers (#172) and Mastra adapters (#173). 3.4.0 is next.
>
> Written 2026-11-04, after 3.2.0. Based on a scan of the npm packages in the same space (download counts for the week ending 2026-11-02, stars from GitHub on 2026-11-04), summarised in section 1. The rows in [PROJECT_ROADMAP.md](PROJECT_ROADMAP.md) track the work; this file explains the choice and order.

## Headline

**3.3 makes the check trustworthy and meets developers where they already are.** It fixes the grounding check's blind spot for negation, corrects the comparison (LlamaIndex.TS is archived), and ships the library as AI SDK middleware, Vitest/Jest matchers and Mastra scorers. **3.4 adds depth:** an opt-in LLM-judge mode, measured guardrails, provider-native citations and a publishable MCP server.

The direction is unchanged: the grounding, evaluation and guardrails layer for RAG in Node.js, used on its own or next to LangChain, the Vercel AI SDK and Mastra.

No JavaScript package has become _the_ RAG evaluation library: the big ones are general-purpose and LLM-judge based, and the RAG-specific ones are each under 1k a week. That is the opening.

**A problem in our own product** (reproduced on the published 3.2.0): the grounding check is lexical. "Full-time employees never receive paid vacation" is scored grounded (1.0) against "Full-time employees receive twenty days of paid vacation per year", and so is "do not receive twenty days". A correct paraphrase ("Staff working full time get 20 days of paid leave annually") is scored ungrounded. Number words already work ("20" matches "twenty"). For a library whose pitch is "answers you can check", the negation case is the first thing to fix, and before the launch posts.

**What we have that others don't**, to lead with: deterministic, free, offline answer checks; a numbers-must-match-the-sources check; `checkAnswer` on other frameworks' output; a RAG-specific eval Action that compares with main; ACL filtering before generation; `RetrievalGuard`, which scans retrieved documents for indirect injection (shipped, but missing from the README); a plugin contract test kit; a 6 MB eval-only install; Workers support tested in workerd.

## 2. 3.3.0: trust the check, meet developers where they are

In order. Each is one pull request with its README, CHANGELOG, roadmap row and docs, as usual.

| #   | Item                            | What                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | Effort |
| --- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| 1   | **Negation in grounding**       | `CitationTracker`, `computeFaithfulness` and `checkAnswer` detect a polarity mismatch between an answer sentence and its best-supporting passage (not, never, no, without, -n't, "no longer"...) and report the sentence as contradicted, not supported. A fixture set of paraphrase, negation and number cases becomes a regression test. Paraphrase stays a documented limit until the judge mode. | S      |
| 2   | **Comparison corrected**        | README "How it compares" and the docs Comparison page: LlamaIndex.TS marked archived, Mastra and the AI SDK added as things you use _with_ this library. A short "Coming from LlamaIndex.TS" guide mapping its retriever, query engine and evaluator to ours. README mentions `RetrievalGuard`.                                                                                                      | S      |
| 3   | **AI SDK grounding middleware** | `groundingMiddleware({ retriever, guardrails, check })` for `wrapLanguageModel`: retrieves and packs context in `transformParams`, then runs ACL, PII redaction and `checkAnswer` in `wrapGenerate` and `wrapStream`, with the result in provider metadata. Works with `generateText` and `streamText`.                                                                                              | M      |
| 4   | **Test-runner matchers**        | `expect(answer).toBeGroundedIn(sources)`, `toCite(sourceId)` and `toContainNoPII()` for Vitest and Jest, from `/testing`, with failure messages that name the unsupported sentences.                                                                                                                                                                                                                 | S      |
| 5   | **Mastra adapters**             | `toMastraScorer(metric)` exposing faithfulness, context recall and numeric consistency as Mastra scorers that need no model calls (useful as a free first pass before Mastra's LLM-judge scorers), and the guardrails as a Mastra input/output processor. In the `/adapters` area next to the AI SDK adapter, with `@mastra/core` as an optional peer.                                               | S      |

Then the release PR, blog post and the launch posts (`release-notes/launch/`), updated to say negation is handled.

## 3. 3.4.0: depth

| Item                              | What                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Effort |
| --------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------ |
| **Opt-in LLM-judge mode**         | `{ judge: llm }` on `checkAnswer` and the evaluator: split the answer into claims, ask any `llm` plugin for a verdict per claim against the sources, return per-claim verdicts. The deterministic check stays the default and runs first; the judge settles what words can't (paraphrase). Judge cost reported. | M      |
| **Measured guardrails**           | `rag-pipeline eval-guardrails labeled.jsonl` reporting precision, recall and F1 for the injection, PII and ACL guards, plus a fixtures pack of RAG attacks (poisoned chunks, indirect injection, fabricated sources). Publish the numbers like the retrieval benchmarks.                                        | M      |
| **Provider-native citations**     | Normalise Anthropic Citations API and OpenAI file-search annotations into `CitationTracker`'s format, then verify them: a citation that exists may still not support the claim.                                                                                                                                 | S–M    |
| **Publishable MCP server**        | `npx @devilsdev/rag-mcp-server ./docs` (a fifth package): index a folder and serve `search_documents` and `check_answer` over stdio. Grows from `examples/mcp-server`; lets the project be listed in MCP directories honestly.                                                                                  | M      |
| **Scores to observability tools** | Evaluation and citation scores as attributes on the existing OpenTelemetry spans, and `toLangfuseScores(result)` mapping to Langfuse's score API. No SaaS dependency in the core.                                                                                                                               | S–M    |
| **Pluggable guard detectors**     | A `detector` contract so a model (Llama Guard, a moderation API, Presidio over HTTP) can replace or add to the pattern-based injection and PII checks.                                                                                                                                                          | M      |
| **Pinecone retriever**            | The connector the roadmap already lists as next after pgvector and Qdrant (`@pinecone-database/pinecone` gets about 1M downloads a week); same contract suite.                                                                                                                                                  | M      |

## 4. Adoption work that isn't a feature

- **Starters:** `npm create rag-pipeline` with Next.js + AI SDK, Mastra and Cloudflare Workers templates (3.4). Mastra credits `npm create mastra` and its templates for much of its onboarding.
- **Integration pages:** after items 3 and 5 land, propose entries for the AI SDK community docs, the Mastra integrations page, and a Langfuse/Phoenix "external evaluation" recipe.
- **A StackBlitz link for every README use case**, including "paste an answer and its sources, see the unsupported sentences".
- **Measure the right things:** dependents, Action users and stars, not raw downloads (the jump from about 90 to 2,124 a week lines up with releases, so mirrors and scanners are in it).

## 5. Not planned

The anti-goals stand: no web UI (local eval viewers like evalite's or Mastra Studio's are answered by the HTML report and the PR comment), no hosted service, no vector database of our own, no agent framework. Code and table chunkers, LLM metadata extraction at ingest and neighbour-chunk expansion have real demand but push the library towards a general framework; reconsider after 3.4.
